transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
The Pentagon is now acknowledging that U.S. casualties in the war with Iran
are higher than previously announced.
That number now stands at 22.
NPR's Quill Lawrence reports.
A Pentagon spokesman told NPR,
"The way casualties are being counted is being standardized,
and that the department will begin posting numbers that are 'pending adjudication'
and may change."
But this is not the first time the Trump Administration
has abruptly posted new numbers
or changed the way it counts casualties from the Iran war,
spreading the numbers of wounded in action,
killed in action, and non-combat casualties
as if they were not part of the same war.
Two leading Democrats on the House Armed Services Committee
said in a statement that while they were glad to see the error had been corrected,
there is "no excuse for a mistake of this magnitude."
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
An attack Saturday on Saudi Arabia's major airport
killed 12 people, including one American,
and wounded more than 300 others.
Saudi officials are blaming Houthi rebels for that assault.
President Trump hosted a rare midterm rally in Tennessee Saturday.
Trump won that state by double digits in 2023.
As Mariana Bakayow from member station WPLN reports,
Trump says his visit is about celebrating the GOP lead in Tennessee.
Trump acknowledged that it's rare for him
to stump for candidates in a ruby red state.
But I said, you know, sometimes it's nice to go to a place
where you don't have to be,
but you're there to say thank you to the great people
that elected you three separate times in record time.
Trump touted the war in Iran
and his decision to deploy the National Guard to Memphis
as he addressed the crowd in Clarksville, Tennessee.
Thousands braved the rain to see his rally, including Laurie Hoskins.
I just didn't know it's going to be close again,
so I always got to say Trump.
Hoskins is one of many voters in the state
that will be voting in a new congressional district this November
after the state re-districted at Trump's behest.
For NPR News, I'm Mariana Bakayow in Nashville.
The public comment period closed this week for a federal proposal
to gut the standards for the nation's largest early education program,
NPR's Sequoia Carillo reports.
The Trump administration's proposed changes to the Head Start program
garnered more than 40,000 comments over the last two months.
The administration says the move to take 133 pages of guidelines
and reduce it to only a handful
is meant to reduce administrative burden on Head Start centers,
but advocates say the move will undermine the program's standard of care.
The six-year-old anti-poverty program provides preschool and childcare
along with meals and support services for qualifying families.
The program serves more than 700,000 kids each year from birth to age five.
The proposal now goes back to the Trump administration to reply to public comment.
Sequoia Carillo, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
Officials in Panama say no deaths have been reported so far
following two major earthquakes on Friday,
but there has been significant structural damage across the entire country.
Most of the damage occurred in the central provinces of Panama.
The Panama Canal, though, remains operational.
The U.S. has pledged $5 million in humanitarian aid.
Some Chesapeake Bay oyster farmers and harvesters are getting a boost from robots,
as NPR's Ari Daniel reports.
An engineer at the University of Maryland is finding new uses for water robots.
Oyster reefs used to abound in the Chesapeake,
but over-harvesting decimated their ranks.
Watermen face the daunting task of knowing when and where to harvest the adults.
Mechanical engineer Miao Yu says the water's so murky
that the effort tends to be a stab in the dark.
Our goal is to transform that guesswork into precision.
So she and her team scan the seabed using sonar and video footage
from a raft-like surface robot and a smaller underwater robot.
They then use AI to stitch the visuals together and analyze them
to determine if oysters are present and alive and how big they are.
They're still refining the algorithms,
but use hoping the technology might one day be modified and scaled nationally.
Ari Daniel, NPR News.
Spain scored twice in the first 14 minutes,
as Spain beat the U.S. women's soccer team Saturday 2-0.
Spain also stopped a second-half penalty kick in the win.
It was the first of two meetings between reigning World Cup champion Spain
and reigning Olympic winner the U.S.
They will be playing once again on Tuesday night near Philadelphia.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Pentagon acknowledges U.S. casualties in Iran war are higher, now 22, pending adjudication
Attack on Saudi Arabia's major airport kills 12 including one American, blamed on Houthi rebels
Trump holds rare midterm rally in Clarksville, Tennessee, touting Iran war and Memphis National Guard deployment
Trump administration proposes gutting Head Start program standards; public comment period closes
Two major earthquakes strike Panama with no reported deaths but significant structural damage
University of Maryland engineer uses robots and AI to locate Chesapeake Bay oysters for harvesters
Spain beats U.S. women's soccer team 2-0 Saturday, stopping a second-half penalty kick
